I’ve been feeling off for a while now—about a year and a half, maybe longer. There were times, like last winter, when I just felt… empty. Like nothing mattered. I stopped caring about my delivery ratings, even though I used to take pride in being fast and reliable. I’d sit in the car between drops, staring at the GPS, not moving. When my dispatcher called, I’d answer slow—like my brain had to climb a hill just to form words. Thinking wore me out fast.

But then, around spring, something shifted. For about three months, I had this unstoppable energy. I’d drive all day, take double shifts, barely sleep—three hours a night, sometimes none—but I didn’t feel tired. I felt great, actually. Like I could keep going forever. I was happy for no reason, just buzzing. I didn’t even notice I wasn’t sleeping.

Yeah, I’ve had bad stuff happen—got held up at gunpoint last year during a delivery. But these bursts of energy and the crashes, the insomnia—it’s not tied to that. They come and go. The trauma’s always there, but these episodes? They feel like their own thing.
D009-D018_h024.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D009-D018_h025.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a long time—like over a year now. There are days when I just feel empty, like nothing matters. I used to care about my playing, but now even nailing a tough passage doesn’t bring me joy. I pace during breaks, can’t sit still, even though I’m exhausted—my arms feel like lead after a concert. I haven’t touched my side projects in months.

But then there are these stretches—like three months last year—where sleep just didn’t matter. I’d stay up composing, practicing, even organizing my whole apartment at 3 a.m. I snapped at my section mate over a tiny tuning thing, which wasn’t like me, but I didn’t care. Felt restless, charged up, like I had five concerts in one day and loved it.

Yeah, I did go through a bad car accident years ago—sometimes I still get flashes—but these mood shifts? They don’t line up with trauma triggers. The irritability, the sleepless bursts—they come and go in waves, totally separate from that. It’s like my mood has its own unpredictable rhythm, not tied to the past. It’s the lows that wreck my work now.
D009-D018_h025.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
